title: Musicians who came around the jitney dances; how jitney dances ran
summary: Ernie names musicians he knew from the jitney halls and fills in for others. He explains how jitney dancing worked, with tickets, a number played right after another and long hours.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you know Papa Wayne? No, I didn't know him too good. I didn't know him too well. I knew the Sharky quite well. I'd been in the Sharky and the Blooms that died. He played drama, so he died. I'd been in the formalities here. And Tony Almericka were quite nice, I'd been in there for quite a long time. And Lloyd Cantor, the bass player. Two or three of them. I know his brothers.
Yeah, I know his brothers. Cousins.
And Jeff, piano player. I used to be around them, because they used to come around with Jitneys too, you see. They'd come around with Jitneys.
Did you ever play anything with, maybe you mentioned it already, the Jitney jobs?
Well, I filled in there, I filled in for Willie Pontio several times when he was at the Budweiser. Oh yeah.

And I'd sit and go around, you know what I'm sitting there. And I'd play several times for Mighty Leigh. You know, still. Played a couple nights in that place. But I didn't go for the Jitneys too much. The hours was so long. They'd go to work, get a clock at night, knock off four o'clock the next morning. No rest. In other words, even the one that's gonna knock off. That's when that man dropped the hanker, that's when they knock off.
Boy gives a pull a coin.

See what they do, see like, like you a drummer and you happen to walk in there. Oh man, come sit down and play a few numbers for me. Well, you ain't playing this week, you feel like playing. You sit down on that drum and play, and he sneak out the back door, and I'll go up Rampo Street somewhere. You got a few hours coming back. See now, you tired after you can't leave without no drum. How did they play those Jitney dancing? One number right after the other. Well, you see, they all have music, see. The music is facing. Play one number and turn it over, and then play the other number and turn it over, and when you get to them, turn it back and start again. But in between that, they say, well, if they're gonna play a five-minute slow drag, and it's not five-minute slow drag with the number they have up there, they play something out the head. Or you can pick up, see, like, I pick up a chorus on a trumpet, and when I finish that chorus, I take down. Piano player take, maybe the saxophone player take it, and the piano player take it. Now as soon as you find that player fair, we go out and the saxophone player pick up the next number just that quick. Soon as soon as soon as he hit the last note, he pick up the next number. See? Well, as soon as he pick up the next number, he might pick up something he say, because I'm planning to leave. When he do that, I got this music on. As soon as he finish, I don't start this number.
Soon that first note hit, the fellow's running around picking up them tickets, the world's behind the tickets.

You see, see, I'm going to this every time they dance, it's a dime, you see, when they got that ticket. Soon as soon as he start that music, he go around and full pick up the tickets, get that number. You see, a man will buy so many tickets.

We got a girl he like to dance, he might buy 50 tickets. That's a long time. And once she just tag, he'd have a ticket off and give her. Soon as the next number starts. And see them tickets like that, the fellow's running around picking up them tickets. It was like that all night long.
